The original text says the normal ocular tests argue against primary retinal or intraocular pathology; the statements capture this, but not the full causal framing that the normal tests are the reason for arguing against those pathologies.

The original text states that no other neurological deficits were found, which is compatible with ocular myasthenia gravis; the statements capture both facts separately but not the explicit compatibility relationship in one statement.

The original text says limitation of adduction, elevation, and depression with ptosis and mydriasis is a classic pattern for left oculomotor nerve palsy; the statements split the movement limitations into separate statements and do not preserve the full classic pattern as a single relationship.
